# Fixed effects
![](images/fixed_effect.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

Fixed effects are any term related to your hypothesis that requires evaluation and any continuous control variables.

We are interested in the differences of our three sites (UD, MD, and LD) so we used it as a fixed effect.
We are also interested in the difference of the media compared ot the environmental sample so we used `Media` as a fixed effect.

To control for the read counts/depths of the samples we used `Reads` as a fixed effect.
This uses it as a continuous control variable.

## Main effect and interactions

When using fixed effects you can look at the main effect, interactions, or both of multiple variables.

The main effects is when looking at the effect of one variable by itself.
Interactions are used to test whether the effect of one predictor variable on the outcome changes depending on another predictor variable.
For example, an interaction between treatment and time point tests whether the treatment effect is different at different time points.

In our formula we specified the formula to only look at main effects.

## Fixed effect specifications

Below is a list of examples on how to specify the usage of fixed effects.

- `a`: Main effect of a
- `a + b`: Main effect of a and b (no interaction)
- `a:b`: Interaction of a and b (no main effects)
- `a * b`: Main effects and interaction of a and b (expands to `a + b + a:b`)
- `(a+b+c)^2`: Main effects and 2-way interactions (no 3-way interaction) of a, b , and c (expands to `a + b + c + a:b + a:c + b:c`)
- `(a+b)*c`: all main effects and pairwise interactions between a and c, and b and c (not between a and b) (expands to `a + b + c + a:c + b:c`)
- `0 + a`: 0 suppresses the intercept resulting in a model that has one parameter per level of a (identical to : a - 1)


::: {.callout-tip}
The `maaslin3()` developers recommend combing 2 fixed effect columns into one for interactions rather than the `a:b` method.
For example, you could use the column `site.media` as a main effect to see the interactions of `Site` and `Media` rather than using `site:media` in the formula.
:::
